lbf.no_crowding.reasoning: Behaviour = the three foragers are bunched together in one cluster instead of dispersing over the 8x8 grid. I measured group dispersion as the MEAN pairwise Manhattan distance between the three agents' (row,col) cells at that step, and labelled 1 when that mean is <= 3 cells. Rationale for the threshold: on an 8x8 grid three uniformly-placed agents sit about 5.3 cells apart on average (grid diameter 14), so a mean of 3 or less means all three are packed into one small neighbourhood - clearly 'bunched' rather than 'spread out'. I used the mean over all three pairs rather than the closest pair, because the sentence is about the group failing to spread out, not about two agents happening to pass each other. Food/score columns were not used: crowding is purely a spatial property of the step.

lbf.no_freeloading.reasoning: Behaviour = at this step at least one agent is contributing nothing to the collecting while the others do, and it is hanging around close to them rather than foraging somewhere else. Two conditions, both checked per step: (a) some agent's cumulative score is still exactly 0 while at least one other agent's score is > 0 (so collecting is demonstrably happening and that agent has had no part in it); (b) that zero-score agent is 'nearby' a scoring agent - I set 'nearby' at Manhattan distance <= 3 cells. Rationale for 3: on an 8x8 grid (diameter 14, random pairwise mean ~5.3) three cells is close enough that the idler is loitering in the same corner of the map as the worker rather than independently searching elsewhere; it is also within a couple of moves of joining a load. Steps before anyone has scored are 0 (nobody is yet 'doing all the collecting'), and steps where the non-scoring agents have wandered far away are 0 (that is not idling NEARBY). Episode 2, where no food is ever collected, is all 0.

walker2d.no_forward_fall.reasoning: rooty is the torso pitch angle. In this data rooty is essentially never positive (max +0.006) and every large excursion is negative, and those negative excursions coincide with rootz (torso height) collapsing from ~1.25 toward ~1.0 while rootx and v_rootx move in the negative direction - i.e. the torso is toppling over in its direction of travel. So negative rooty is the 'forward' pitch direction here, and I label on rooty being past a negative threshold. Threshold: rooty <= -0.5 rad (~29 deg). Rationale: Walker2d's healthy pitch band is |rooty| < 1.0, at which point the walker is already down; the description asks for 'the angle that PRECEDES a face-first fall', so I took half of the terminal angle. That matches the data - in episodes 1, 2 and 3 the torso height only starts dropping in earnest right around the step where rooty crosses -0.5, and it never recovers afterwards. Episode 0 (which stays above -0.30 and keeps its height) gets no positives. Only the instantaneous angle is used, not the angular velocity, since the sentence is about being past an angle.

lunarlander.no_tilt.reasoning: The sentence has two parts and I require both at the step: the lander is DESCENDING (vy < 0) and it is at a STEEP tilt (|angle| > 0.2 rad, about 11.5 deg). Rationale for 0.2 rad: 'keep the lander close to upright' is a tight requirement, and ~11-12 deg is about the point where a lander can no longer set both legs down cleanly and its main engine thrust is pushing it sideways rather than braking the fall; below that it still reads as roughly upright. Sign of the angle is irrelevant - a steep lean either way breaks 'upright' - so I used the absolute value. Requiring vy < 0 matters because the description is specifically about descending at a tilt; in practice episode 1 is the only one that ever gets steep, and it is descending throughout, so it turns on at t=14 (angle 0.204) and stays on. Episodes 0, 2 and 3 never exceed 0.13 rad and are all 0.

cartpole.left_only.reasoning: Behaviour = the pole is being balanced AND the cart is on the left half of the track, so I require both at the step. 'Left half of the track': CartPole's track runs from -2.4 to +2.4, so the left half is cart_position < 0 (the midpoint, 0, is the natural split; there is nothing vague about it). 'Balanced': the pole is still up, i.e. |pole_angle| <= 0.2095 rad (12 deg), which is CartPole-v1's own failure angle - past it the pole is falling, not being balanced. In these episodes the angle never quite reaches 12 deg (largest is 0.205 at the final recorded step of episode 3), because the logs stop at termination, so in practice the labels follow cart_position < 0: episode 0 turns on at t=15 when the cart crosses to the left, episode 1 is on for its first five steps only, episode 2 is entirely on the right half and is all 0, and episode 3 is on the left throughout.
